title: Revenue Integrity Standard: Duplicate Reservations and Per-Ticket Entitlements
content:
**Revenue integrity standard — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** Tickets held by one customer are evaluated together only for duplicate protection, and never pool their entitlements.

## Duplicate reservations

A customer may not hold two reservations for the same passenger name that are both held or ticketed with the same origin, destination and first scheduled departure; the second such reservation is not created. The test is made on the system records of the customer's reservations: same customer, same passenger name, same origin, same destination, same first scheduled departure, and both reservations held or ticketed. Where two such reservations already exist, only the one with the earlier booking moment may be ticketed, and the later one is left to lapse.

| Existing reservation for the same passenger (hypothetical) | New reservation, same origin, destination and first departure |
|---|---|
| Held | Not created |
| Ticketed | Not created |
| Different first scheduled departure | Not a duplicate under this standard |

## Entitlements stay on their own ticket

Baggage allowances, seat entitlements, fee waivers and residual values belong to the individual ticket on which they arise. They are never transferred to, added to or netted against another ticket of the same customer, and a waiver used on one ticket never reduces the waivers available on another.

*Hypothetical case.* A customer holds two Crestline Premium Economy tickets. The free bags of the first ticket cannot be used on the second, and a residual left on one ticket is not set against a fare difference on the other.
